question.text: Will Plus Ultra operate a scheduled Madrid–Lima passenger flight on 26 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if Plus Ultra's regularly scheduled Madrid–Barajas (MAD) to Lima (LIM) passenger service operated with a scheduled departure date of 26 November 2026 — i.e. Flightradar24's flight history for flight PU301 (https://www.flightradar24.com/data/flights/pu301) shows a recorded departure for that date (an actual departure time, or status "Landed"/"Delayed"), or an equivalent PU-numbered flight on that route is shown operating that day. A flight that took off from Madrid for Lima but subsequently diverted, returned or was turned back still counts as operated. It resolves NO if no Plus Ultra flight departed Madrid for Lima on 26 November 2026, including if such a flight was cancelled, removed from the schedule, or the route had already been suspended. If Flightradar24 does not list the flight in question, the same determination will be made using Airportia's Plus Ultra flight list (https://www.airportia.com/airlines/plus-ultra/) or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
question.fine_print: "26 November 2026" means the Europe/Madrid calendar date of the scheduled departure from Madrid; a departure slipping past midnight still counts toward its scheduled date. Only Plus Ultra's regular scheduled Madrid–Lima passenger service counts — including when flown with a wet-leased aircraft and including flights whose seats were already sold before Plus Ultra stopped selling the route. Ad-hoc charter, cargo, positioning, maintenance and technical-stop flights do not count.

research:
I couldn't confirm whether Plus Ultra will fly Madrid-Lima on Thursday 26 November. Flightradar24, Airportia and other trackers all blocked me, and no source gives a date for the last Lima flight. The latest report (16 November) says the route is still running normally.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: Flightradar24's PU301 page returned HTTP 403 (a Cloudflare bot check), so I could not read the flight history or schedule. I also could not find a data file behind the page. [FR24](https://www.flightradar24.com/data/flights/pu301)
- 2026-11-16: Airportia's Plus Ultra page, FlightAware (PUE301) and Flightera were also blocked (403). [Airportia](https://www.airportia.com/airlines/plus-ultra/)
- The background says that as of 13 November, FR24 listed PU301 departures only up to 20 November. I could not check whether 26 November has since appeared on FR24. A schedule that stops on the 20th could just mean FR24 doesn't show dates that far ahead yet, or it could mean the flights have been taken out of the schedule.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The airline has not announced a last flight date, and I found no report that the 26 November flight has been cancelled.
- 2026-11-16: T News (Peru) says Plus Ultra keeps flying to Lima "normally and on time": the previous day's flight arrived on time, with no cancellations or delays. The end date is still unknown and there is no official timetable for stopping. [T News](https://tnews.com.pe/vuelos-de-plus-ultra-siguen-llegando-a-lima/)
- **Thursday looks like a scheduled day, but the background overstates the frequency.** A 25 September update to the airline's website removed Tuesday Lima flights from 13 October and Saturday flights from 7 November. That leaves about 5 flights a week, not daily except Tuesday. Thursday still appears to be one of them. [Demócrata](https://www.democrata.es/actualidad/plus-ultra-suspende-rutas-lima-buenos-aires-hacer-si-tienes-billete-como-reclamar-dinero/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: Periodista Digital describes Plus Ultra as "on the brink of bankruptcy". It has repaid none of the €53m SEPI loan and asked for a two-year extension. [Periodista Digital](https://www.periodistadigital.com/economia/20261116/plus-ultra-borde-quiebra-video-689405267390/)
- 2026-11-15: Demócrata says the sales halt "does not mean all flights already booked are cancelled". The airline plans to suspend the routes "soon", but no final cancellation date has been given for pending flights. [Demócrata](https://www.democrata.es/actualidad/plus-ultra-suspende-rutas-lima-buenos-aires-hacer-si-tienes-billete-como-reclamar-dinero/)
- 2026-11-15: Europa Press reports the Plus Ultra court case continues during the election campaign. [Europa Press](https://www.europapress.es/nacional/noticia-tribunales-no-paran-campana-electoral-declaraciones-casos-leire-koldo-plus-ultra-ceuta-20261115125957.html)
- 2026-11-13: T News: no date has been set for leaving Lima, "not in days, weeks or months", according to its sources. A Madrid-Lima flight left on time that Friday. The airline had not confirmed the sales halt. Plus Ultra carried 16,349 passengers to Lima in July (Peru's civil aviation authority, DGAC). [T News](https://tnews.com.pe/no-hay-fecha-para-que-plus-ultra-deje-lima/)
- 2026-11-13: El Comercio (citing ABC) says the Lima and Buenos Aires routes and their ticket sales were cancelled, with no date given. Caracas routes are kept as profitable. [El Comercio](https://elcomercio.pe/economia/peru/plus-ultra-entra-en-preconcurso-de-acreedores-aerolinea-dejaria-de-operar-en-lima-l-ultimas-noticia/)
- 2026-11-13: El Economista headline: Plus Ultra is suspending all flights except Venezuela. [El Economista](https://www.eleconomista.es/transportes-turismo/noticias/14027551/11/26/plus-ultra-suspende-todos-sus-vuelos-salvo-venezuela-y-prepara-preconcurso-de-acreedores-y-un-erte-para-mas-de-500-trabajadores.html)
- 2026-11-13: El Cronista: no official date for ending Buenos Aires operations either. [El Cronista](https://www.cronista.com/negocios/a-medio-ano-de-aterrizar-en-la-argentina-una-aerolinea-espanola-suspende-todos-sus-vuelos-al-pais/)
- Other coverage I found but could not fully read: [Sir Chandler](https://www.sirchandler.com.ar/2026/11/en-espana-informan-que-plus-ultra-dejaria-de-volar-a-buenos-aires/) (an intention to stop both routes, no definitive date), [Tourinews](https://www.tourinews.es/empresas-turismo/plus-ultra-suspende-ventas-vuelos-hacia-buenos-aires-lima_4495567_102.html) and [Vozpópuli](https://www.vozpopuli.com/economia/empresas/plus-ultra-se-queda-sin-financiacion-privada-prepara-despidos-y-el-cierre-de-rutas-para-sobrevivir.html).

## 4. Base rates
- I found no systematic data on how long an airline keeps flying a route after it stops selling tickets. In past airline failures it has ranged from same-day grounding to several weeks of flights for people who had already booked.
- Demócrata notes that giving passengers at least 14 days' notice generally removes the airline's duty to pay fixed EU261 compensation (up to €600). 13 November plus 14 days is 27 November, so cancelling a 26 November flight now would fall short of that. The airline would still owe refunds or rebooking. [Demócrata](https://www.democrata.es/actualidad/plus-ultra-suspende-rutas-lima-buenos-aires-hacer-si-tienes-billete-como-reclamar-dinero/)
- Plus Ultra has cut gradually before: Tuesday Lima flights went in October and Saturdays on 7 November, each announced weeks ahead. The Bogotá route was suspended in October.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the prediction market listings supplied matches this question; they cover unrelated topics. I found no Polymarket, Manifold or Metaculus market on Plus Ultra's routes.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Any announcement from Plus Ultra or the court of a last Lima flight date, or emails to passengers about cancellations.
- ERE (collective dismissal) consultations with the unions, and preconcurso (pre-insolvency) talks under the Madrid commercial court no. 8. If the airline moves to full insolvency (concurso), as the UGT union warns could happen, flying could stop abruptly.
- Possible deal with Iberojet (Grupo Barceló).
- Spanish general election on 29 November (after the flight date) and court hearings in the Plus Ultra case.
- Scheduled Lima departures on 18, 19, 20, 22, 23 and 25 November will show whether the route is still running. Whether 26 November appears on FR24 is the most direct thing to watch.

Yes prices: Victor Wembanyama: 0.55; Jayson Tatum: 0.15; Luka Dončić: 0.24; Aaron Gordon: 0.0100; Allen Graves: 0.0100; Aday Mara: 0.0100; Ajay Mitchell: 0.8500; Andrew Nembhard: 0.8500; Aaron Nesmith: 0.0000; Austin Reaves: 0.0000.

- Kalshi: Lima Mayor winner? (in 2026). Yes prices: Rafael López Aliaga: 0.07; Alberto Tejada: 0.0100; Daniel Urresti: 0.0100; Luis Rubio: 0.0100; Oswaldo Vargas: 0.0100; Ricardo Belmont: 0.0100; Yehude Simon: 0.0100; Susel Paredes: 0.0100; Carlos Bruce: 0.0300; Francis Allison: 0.0200.
- Kalshi: Will nonstop U.S.–Lebanon passenger flights resume? (a publicly scheduled commercial passenger flight carrying revenue passengers completes a nonstop trip between an airport in the United States and an airport in Lebanon). Yes prices: Before Apr 1, 2027: 0.28; Before Jan 1, 2027: 0.06.
- Kalshi: Will U.S. direct flights to Russia resume? (Before 2027). Yes prices: Before 2027: 0.02; Before 2026: 0.0100.
- Kalshi: 151 Ultra-Premium Collection Up or Down: November ( | 151 Ultra-Premium Collection). Yes prices: Above $832.19: 0.38.

**Bottom line:** As of 16 November 2026 the question is not settled. Plus Ultra's Madrid-Lima flights were still flying normally up to 16 November, and no last-flight date has been announced. But the airline stopped selling the route on 13 November and says it is giving it up. I could not find any public schedule that shows a flight on 26 November, either confirmed or cancelled.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: The Flightradar24 PU301 page blocked me (HTTP 403, Cloudflare check). Airportia's Plus Ultra page also returned 403, so I could not read either named source directly. [FR24](https://www.flightradar24.com/data/flights/pu301), [Airportia](https://www.airportia.com/airlines/plus-ultra/)
- 2026-11-16: FlightStats, used instead, shows PU301 Madrid 11:00 to Lima 17:10 scheduled on 13, 15, 16, 18 and 19 November, with no flight on Saturday 14 or Tuesday 17. Its window ends on 19 November. When I asked it for 26 November it returned the same 13-19 November view, so I could not see whether a 26 November flight is still scheduled. [FlightStats](https://www.flightstats.com/v2/flight-tracker/PU*/301)
- 2026-11-13: The question background says FR24 then listed PU301 departures up to 20 November, which may only reflect how far ahead FR24 shows schedules. I could not check this.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The route is still operating, ticket sales are closed, and there is no official end date.
- 2026-11-16: T News (Peru) says a Madrid-Lima flight reached Lima on schedule on 15 November, another was crossing the Atlantic on 16 November, and there were no cancellations or delays. It adds that the end date "could be known at any moment." [T News](https://tnews.com.pe/vuelos-de-plus-ultra-siguen-llegando-a-lima/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: RTVC (Canary Islands TV) says Plus Ultra has stopped scheduling Lima and other routes "for the coming months" and says it is still operating. A Canarian-Venezuelan association says route cancellations "have already begun." [RTVC](https://rtvc.es/plus-ultra-anuncia-recortes-rutas-prepara-despidos-16-noviembre-2026)
- 2026-11-16: Periodista Digital reports the airline is "on the brink of bankruptcy." The SEPI loan principal is still unpaid, and Plus Ultra has asked for a two-year extension. [Periodista Digital](https://www.periodistadigital.com/economia/20261116/plus-ultra-borde-quiebra-video-689405267390/)
- 2026-11-15: Que.es lists Lima among the suspended routes and tells ticket holders to contact the airline. [Que.es](https://www.que.es/2026/11/15/plus-ultra-preconcurso-acreedores-rutas/)

- 2026-11-13: El Comercio, citing ABC and the airline's court filing, says Plus Ultra "cancelled routes and ticket sales" to Lima and Buenos Aires and kept Caracas. It gives no date. [El Comercio](https://elcomercio.pe/economia/peru/plus-ultra-entra-en-preconcurso-de-acreedores-aerolinea-dejaria-de-operar-en-lima-l-ultimas-noticia/)
- 2026-11-13: Deep Arrival, citing La Nación, says Peru bookings were removed from the website and the airline did not answer questions about existing bookings. [Deep Arrival](https://deeparrival.com/news/plus-ultra-679-job-cuts-lima-buenos-aires-tickets/)
- 2026-11-13: Tourinews reports the sales suspension. [Tourinews](https://www.tourinews.es/empresas-turismo/plus-ultra-suspende-ventas-vuelos-hacia-buenos-aires-lima_4495567_102.html), [Sir Chandler](https://www.sirchandler.com.ar/2026/11/en-espana-informan-que-plus-ultra-dejaria-de-volar-a-buenos-aires/)
- 2026-10-09: When Plus Ultra cut Buenos Aires frequencies, passengers complained of being stranded and of getting vouchers or new dates rather than rebooking on other airlines. This suggests the airline may cancel already-sold flights instead of flying them. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/economia/2026/10/09/plus-ultra-redujo-sus-vuelos-a-madrid-y-los-pasajeros-denuncian-estar-varados-comenzo-a-volar-en-el-pais-hace-apenas-4-meses/)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026-05-06: Plus Ultra announced its Colombia suspension effective 2 June, about four weeks' notice, and kept flying until then. [Diario Libre](https://www.diariolibre.com/mundo/america-latina/2026/05/06/plus-ultra-suspende-vuelos-a-colombia-por-aumento-de-costos/3525658), [RCN](https://www.noticiasrcn.com/economia/plus-ultra-suspende-operaciones-en-colombia-desde-el-2-de-junio-1018833)
- 2026-10/11: Buenos Aires went from five weekly flights to two. Lima reportedly went from seven to five weekly between October and November, so already-sold flights have been consolidated before. [search summary, iProfesional](https://www.iprofesional.com/actualidad/466337-plus-ultra-redujo-sus-vuelos-a-madrid-y-mas-de-200-pasajeros-no-saben-si-podran-viajar)
- The 26 November flight is 13 days after sales stopped. I did not find a figure for how often this airline flies already-sold flights after stopping sales. More generally, airlines in this situation often keep flying for a few weeks to clear booked passengers, but some cancel quickly to save cash.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied Kalshi markets matches this question; they cover a Lima mayor race, other flight routes, sports and collectibles. I found no Polymarket, Manifold or Metaculus forecast on Plus Ultra's Lima route.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- An announcement of the last Lima flight date could come at any time, according to T News on 16 November.
- 18-19 November: whether FlightStats or FR24 add 22-26 November flights to PU301 as their schedule windows roll forward. Re-checking FlightStats about a week out (from roughly 19-20 November) would show whether 26 November appears as scheduled.
- Pre-insolvency talks before Madrid Mercantile Court No. 8 and the start of union consultations on the 679 job cuts.
- A possible full insolvency filing (UGT warns this is possible) or a deal with Iberojet.
- 29 November: Spanish general election, after the resolution date. The Plus Ultra court case hearings fall during the campaign.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The outcome is known in about 10 days. For Yes, Plus Ultra's PU301 (or an equivalent PU flight) must actually depart Madrid for Lima with a scheduled date of Thursday 26 November 2026. The route has to survive until then, and that specific flight must not be cancelled.

(b) Status quo: the route is still flying normally (on-time arrivals reported 13, 15 and 16 November), and Thursday remains a scheduled day. If nothing changes, the flight operates and the question resolves Yes. The status quo is fragile, though, because sales stopped on 13 November and the airline says it will drop the route.

(c) Base rate: when a carrier stops selling a route but has not set an end date, it usually keeps flying already-booked passengers for some weeks. Plus Ultra itself gave about 4 weeks' notice for its Colombia suspension and kept flying until then. Distressed carriers sometimes consolidate or cancel quickly instead, as Plus Ultra did with the Buenos Aires frequency cuts, which stranded passengers. Probability that the route is still operating 13 days after a sales halt: roughly 55-65%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - T News, 16 November: flights are "normal and on time", with no cancellations.
  - T News, 13 November: its sources had no departure date, "not in days, weeks or months".
  - EU261: cancelling now with less than 14 days' notice triggers compensation of up to €600 per passenger. Any cancellation announced from today would only reach 14 days' notice in early December.
  - The airline says it aims to protect continuity, and an ERE consultation takes weeks.
  - FR24 showing flights only up to 20 November likely just reflects how far ahead it displays schedules.
- **For No:**
  - Sales were halted entirely on 13 November. If the end date were far off, the airline would likely have kept selling up to it.
  - El Economista (13 November): all flights except Venezuela are being suspended.
  - RTVC (16 November): a Canarian-Venezuelan association says cancellations "have already begun".
  - The airline faces acute liquidity stress, fuel costs up about 68% and a possible full insolvency.
  - It has consolidated already-sold flights before (Lima Tuesdays and Saturdays, Buenos Aires).
  - About 4% risk that the single flight is cancelled for operational reasons.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** Around 18-20 November Plus Ultra announces that its last Lima flight is 22 or 23 November and rebooks or refunds the remaining passengers to save cash. Alternatively, the Iberojet talks collapse and a concurso forces abrupt cuts.
- **Yes:** The airline sets the last Lima flight for late November or mid-December to clear existing bookings and limit EU261 exposure. PU301 departs on 26 November as scheduled.

(f) I start from about 60% and leave it there. Continued normal operations, with no cancellation news as of 16 November, and the EU261 notice incentive push slightly up. The complete sales halt, signalling a near-term end, plus the airline's cash desperation and its history of consolidating flights push slightly down. These roughly cancel out. There is no relevant prediction market to anchor on.

Probability: 57%

**(a) Time left and what Yes requires.** About 10 days remain. Yes requires PU301 (or an equivalent PU flight) to actually depart Madrid for Lima on Thursday 26 November, as recorded on Flightradar24, Airportia or credible sources.

**(b) Status quo.** The route is flying normally, with on-time departures through 16 November. No cancellation of the 26 November flight and no last-flight date has been announced. Thursday remains a scheduled day even after the Tuesday and Saturday cuts. If nothing changes, the flight operates: Yes.

**(c) Base rate.** Airlines that stop selling a route but keep flying it often run off booked passengers for weeks. Plus Ultra itself gave about 4 weeks' notice before its Colombia exit. Distressed carriers in pre-insolvency, however, sometimes cancel already-sold flights abruptly to save cash. For a flight 13 days after the sales halt, with no end date announced, I put the base rate around 50-60% Yes.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
- For Yes:
  - Flights operated normally on 13, 15 and 16 November (T News).
  - T News sources (13 November) said there was "no date, not in days, weeks or months."
  - Cancelling now, with less than 14 days' notice, risks EU261 compensation of up to €600 per passenger.
  - Fleet reduction and lease returns take time.
  - The Buenos Aires reduced schedule was planned through 13 December.
- For No:
  - Sales stopped on 13 November, and the airline is cutting more than 61% of flight hours with "definitive suspension" of routes.
  - Its liquidity is acute, with fuel costs up about 68%.
  - RTVC (16 November) said a Canarian-Venezuelan association reports cancellations "have already begun."
  - During the October Buenos Aires cuts, Plus Ultra cancelled already-sold flights and offered vouchers.
  - T News said the end date "could be known at any moment."

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No: In the coming days the airline notifies passengers that the last Lima flight is around 20-25 November, consolidating loads to save cash. Alternatively, the creditor talks fail and the airline enters a full concurso, grounding flights abruptly.
- Yes: The airline flies off its booked inventory through late November or December to limit refund and compensation liabilities, announcing a last flight in early or mid December.

**(f) From base rate to forecast.** I start at about 55%. The status quo and the 14-day notice incentive push slightly up. The acute cash crisis, the explicit plan to exit, and the airline's history of cancelling sold flights push down. On balance I land near the middle, leaning slightly toward Yes.

Probability: 52%

(a) The outcome will be known in about 10 days, on 26 November 2026. For Yes, Plus Ultra's PU301 (or an equivalent PU flight) must actually depart Madrid for Lima with a scheduled departure date of Thursday 26 November, shown on FR24, Airportia or credible sources.

(b) If nothing changed, the answer would be Yes. The route is flying normally: flights ran on 13, 15 and 16 November, and FlightStats lists Thursday 19 November as scheduled. Thursday is one of the roughly five weekly Lima days (Wed, Thu, Fri, Sun, Mon). No cancellation of 26 November has been reported.

(c) Base rate: when a distressed airline stops selling a route but has no announced end date, how often does a flight 13 days later still operate? Airlines usually keep flying for 2 to 6 weeks to clear booked passengers and avoid refund and compensation costs. Some instead consolidate frequencies or ground abruptly. Plus Ultra gave about 4 weeks' notice for Colombia and several weeks for earlier frequency cuts. I put the base rate around 60%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - The route was operating "normally and on time" as of 16 November (T News).
  - T News sources (13 November) said there was no exit date "in days, weeks or months".
  - A sales halt does not cancel booked flights (Demócrata, 15 November).
  - Cancelling within 14 days of the flight triggers EU261 compensation. Notice given today already falls short of 14 days for 26 November, which is a cost the airline would want to avoid.
  - The ERE consultation period will run past late November, so crew and aircraft remain available.
  - Lima is a large route (16k passengers in July) with many bookings ahead of Christmas.
- **For No:**
  - Sales stopped on 13 November, and El Economista said "all flights except Venezuela" were being suspended.
  - RTVC (16 November) says Lima is no longer scheduled "for the coming months", and a Venezuelan association says cancellations "have already begun".
  - The airline is cash-starved, with jet fuel up about 68%.
  - During the October Buenos Aires cuts, the airline cancelled sold flights and offered vouchers.
  - A full insolvency filing (concurso) could halt operations abruptly.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** Within days, Plus Ultra announces a last Lima flight around 22 to 25 November, or consolidates remaining passengers onto fewer weekly flights and drops Thursday. Alternatively, a sudden concurso grounds the non-Venezuela flying.
- **Yes:** The airline sets a last flight date in early or mid-December to repatriate already-booked passengers, and the Thursday 26 November flight operates as scheduled.

(f) I start at about 60%. I move down for the airline's acute cash crisis and its record of cancelling sold flights through consolidation, which puts Thursday specifically at risk. I partly offset that with the strong status quo, the 14-day compensation logic and the lack of any announced end date. Net, I move down about 5 points.

Probability: 55%

(a) The outcome will be known by about 26-27 November, roughly 10 days from now. YES requires Plus Ultra's PU301 (or an equivalent PU flight) to actually depart Madrid for Lima on Thursday 26 November and be recorded on Flightradar24, Airportia or credible sources.

(b) The status quo is that the route is still flying normally (on-time flights on 13, 15 and 16 November), and Thursday is still a scheduled day. If nothing changed, the outcome would be YES. But the airline has stopped selling the route and says it will give it up, so the status quo is under strain.

(c) Reference class: routes an airline has stopped selling ahead of a stated exit, while it is in pre-insolvency but not grounded. Flying already-sold flights for 2 to 4 weeks after the sales halt is common. Plus Ultra itself gave about 4 weeks' notice for Colombia and kept flying until the end date. Abrupt cancellation within about two weeks, or a full grounding, happens in perhaps 35-45% of cases. Base rate for a flight about 13 days after the sales halt: about 55-60% YES.

(d) Evidence for YES:
- 16 November: T News reports flights arriving on time with no cancellations, and the end date unknown.
- 13 November: T News sources say there is no exit timeline "in days, weeks or months".
- Cancelling within 14 days of the 26 November flight triggers EU261 compensation of up to €600 per passenger, on top of refunds.
- Passengers already in Lima need return flights, and rebooking them on other airlines is costly.
- The Buenos Aires reduced schedule ran through 13 December, which suggests schedules were already planned into December.

Evidence for NO:
- 13 November: sales halted, and the El Economista headline said it was "suspending all flights except Venezuela".
- The restructuring cuts more than 61% of flight hours, and fuel costs are up sharply, so the airline has a strong incentive to save cash.
- RTVC (16 November) quotes a Canarian-Venezuelan association saying cancellations "have already begun".
- With the Buenos Aires cuts in October, the airline consolidated already-sold flights and stranded passengers.
- UGT warns that a full insolvency (concurso) could stop operations abruptly.
- An end-date announcement "could come at any moment", and it could fall before 26 November.

(e) NO scenario: Around 18-20 November, Plus Ultra announces that the last Lima flight is about 22-25 November and moves remaining passengers onto Caracas-linked aircraft or refunds them. Alternatively, a liquidity crunch forces the airline into full insolvency and it is grounded.
YES scenario: The airline sets an exit at the end of November or in mid-December to carry passengers already booked and to avoid EU261 compensation, and PU301 departs on the 26th as normal.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 57%. I move slightly down for the acute cash crisis, the explicit "suspension" framing and the airline's record of consolidating sold flights. The EU261 timing and the continued normal operation offset part of that. I end up at about 52%.
